title: AI-stock rebound likely came too late to rescue hedge funds' July
excerpt: AI stocks jumped after Citadel bought Leopold Aschenbrenner's stock portfolio. But the rebound likely came too late to rescue other hedge funds' July.
content_html:
Leopold Aschenbrenner’s meltdown helped AI stocks soar. It likely came too late to save other funds’ July returns.

By Bradley Saacks

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

After a banner first half of the year for many big-name, tech-focused hedge funds, July's been a sobering stretch.

Popular artificial-intelligence-linked stocks like SanDisk, Bloom Energy, and CoreWeave tanked in mid-July amid jitters in Asian markets. Mega-cap stocks like Google and Meta faced minor sell-offs as they continue to increase spending on AI and compute capabilities, with nearly all of the companies' free cash being allocated to the trend. Large chipmakers such as TSMC and Micron were dragged down.

As the industry was waiting until the first week of August to see just how bad July had been, a massive market event disrupted the steady downward trend in these stocks.

After weeks of steep losses and margin calls from bank partners, OpenAI researcher turned hedge fund investor Leopold Aschenbrenner was forced to sell the bulk of his publicly traded equity holdings. Situational Awareness's unloading sent many of the aforementioned names soaring, benefiting Citadel, which beat out Millennium and Jane Street to purchase the stock portfolio.

The rebound was a welcome relief, but for many hedge funds that owned the same names, it likely arrived too late to save many funds' months. (That being said, these funds might still be up on the year thanks to their strong first halves. Despite losing 67% in July, Situational Awareness year-to-date returns are still 80%, according to a person familiar with the fund.) The holdings referenced below are from the end of the first quarter, and funds may have bought more or sold some or all of their stakes in recent months.

Whale Rock Capital, the Boston-based tech investor run by Alex Sacerdote, was up more than 70% in the first half, driven by many of the same stocks that dragged down Situational Awareness in recent weeks.

The $19 billion firm added to its stakes in SanDisk and Bloom Energy in the first quarter, according to regulatory filings. Both stocks jumped more than 20% on Thursday, but as of midday Friday, SanDisk remained roughly 45% below where it started July, while Bloom Energy was still down about 30%.

Gavin Baker's Atreides Management and Brad Gerstner's Altimeter Capital both added to their CoreWeave positions in the first quarter, a holding Situational Awareness also had significant exposure to. The cloud computing company was up more than 20% on Thursday after the portfolio sale, but the rebound erased only a fraction of the stock's losses in July.

Tiger Cubs — named for their connection to late billionaire Julian Robertson's Tiger Management — had a resurgent first half, in part due to the AI trade. Funds like Coatue, Tiger Global, Maverick, and Light Street all counted tech companies as their biggest holdings as of the end of the first quarter.

Even mega-cap companies got a boost in the frenzied buying following the Situational Awareness meltdown, despite not being in Aschenbrenner's portfolio. Chipmaker TSMC, a big holding of Coatue, Maverick, Tiger Global, and Light Street, erased roughly a quarter of its July losses Thursday. Lam Research, which produces parts used in semiconductor manufacturing, was up more than 10% on Thursday but will likely end July down close to 30%. The company is a holding of Coatue, Tiger Global, and Whale Rock.

Tiger Global, Whale Rock, and Light Street declined to comment. Atreides, Maverick, Coatue, and Altimeter did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

content_html_zh:
利奥波德·阿申布伦纳 (Leopold Aschenbrenner) 的崩溃帮助人工智能股票飙升。 这可能为时已晚，无法挽救其他基金 7 月份的回报。

作者：Bradley Saacks 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

对于许多知名的、以科技为重点的对冲基金来说，上半年表现出色，但 7 月份却是一个发人深省的时期。

由于亚洲市场的动荡，SanDisk、Bloom Energy 和 CoreWeave 等热门人工智能相关股票在 7 月中旬暴跌。 像谷歌和 Meta 这样的大型股票面临着小幅抛售，因为它们继续增加在人工智能和计算能力上的支出，几乎所有公司的自由现金都分配给了这一趋势。 台积电、美光等大型芯片制造商受到拖累。

由于业界一直等到 8 月的第一周才知道 7 月的情况到底有多糟糕，一场大规模的市场事件扰乱了这些股票的稳步下跌趋势。

在经历了数周的巨额亏损和银行合作伙伴的追加保证金通知后，OpenAI 研究员、转型为对冲基金投资者的利奥波德·阿申布伦纳 (Leopold Aschenbrenner) 被迫出售其持有的大部分公开交易股票。 Situational Awareness 的抛售使得上述许多公司股价飙升，Citadel 受益，它击败了 Millennium 和 Jane Street 购买了该股票投资组合。

反弹令人欣慰，但对于许多同名对冲基金来说，它可能来得太晚了，无法挽救许多基金的几个月。 （话虽如此，由于上半年表现强劲，这些基金今年的表现可能仍会上涨。 据一位熟悉该基金的人士透露，尽管 7 月份损失了 67%，但 Situational Awareness 年初至今的回报率仍为 80%。） 下面引用的持股量来自第一季度末，近几个月来基金可能购买了更多或出售了部分或全部股份。

由 Alex Sacerdote 经营的总部位于波士顿的科技投资者 Whale Rock Capital 上半年股价上涨超过 70%，受到近几周拖累 Situational Awareness 的许多股票的推动。

根据监管文件，这家价值 190 亿美元的公司在第一季度增持了 SanDisk 和 Bloom Energy 的股份。 周四，两只股票均上涨超过 20%，但截至周五中午，SanDisk 仍比 7 月初的水平低约 45%，而 Bloom Energy 仍下跌约 30%。

加文·贝克 (Gavin Baker) 的 Atreides Management 和布拉德·格斯特纳 (Brad Gerstner) 的 Altimeter Capital 均在第一季度增持了 CoreWeave 持仓，而 Situational Awareness 也持有该公司的重要股份。 周四，在出售投资组合后，这家云计算公司股价上涨了 20% 以上，但反弹仅抵消了该股 7 月份跌幅的一小部分。

Tiger Cubs 因其与已故亿万富翁朱利安·罗伯逊 (Julian Robertson) 的老虎管理公司 (Tiger Management) 的联系而得名，上半年业绩复苏，部分原因在于人工智能交易。 截至第一季度末，Coatue、Tiger Global、Maverick 和 Light Street 等基金都将科技公司视为其最大持股。

即使是大型公司，尽管不属于阿申布伦纳的投资组合，但在态势感知崩溃之后，也受到了疯狂买盘的提振。 芯片制造商台积电是 Coatue、Maverick、Tiger Global 和 Light Street 的大股东，该公司周四抹去了 7 月份亏损的约四分之一。 Lam Research 生产用于半导体制造的零部件，周四股价上涨超过 10%，但 7 月底可能下跌近 30%。 该公司是 Coatue、Tiger Global 和 Whale Rock 的控股公司。

Tiger Global、Whale Rock 和 Light Street 拒绝置评。 Atreides、Maverick、Coatue 和 Altimeter 没有立即回应置评请求。

Bradley Saacks 为纽约《商业内幕》报道对冲基金和其他资产管理公司的报道。 他于 2018 年底首次在纽约为《商业内幕》撰写有关价值数万亿美元行业的文章，此前他花了两年时间为《金融时报》的商业出版物《Ignites》报道共同基金。从 2022 年中期开始，他离开《商业内幕》一年多一点，并在媒体初创公司 Semafor 担任商业记者。 他于 2023 年重新加入《商业内幕》，这次是在该出版物的伦敦办事处，此后又搬回纽约。 他毕业于北卡罗来纳大学教堂山分校媒体与新闻学院，曾获得 O.J.
